sets.title: JNVST-style mock test 1
sets.description: A timed mixed test in the order of the JNVST paper: reasoning, environmental studies, arithmetic and a reading passage. Shorter than the real 2-hour paper, and the reasoning questions are text-based, while the real Mental Ability test uses figures.

passages.title: The kite festival
passages.text: Arjun and his grandmother sat on the roof on the morning of Makar Sankranti. The sky was already filled with kites of every colour. Arjun's kite was a small green one that his grandmother had helped him make from paper and thin sticks of bamboo. "Hold the string loosely when the wind is strong," she told him, "and pull it gently when the wind is weak." Arjun followed her advice, and soon his green kite was flying higher than the big red kite of his neighbour. When the sun set, he carefully rolled up the string so that it would not tangle, and promised to fly the kite again the next year.

questions.prompt: What comes next? 5, 10, 20, 40, ?

questions.explanation: A bird lives in a nest; a bee lives in a hive.

questions.explanation: Mars looks reddish because of iron-rich dust on its surface.

questions.explanation: Evaporation is liquid water turning into water vapour.

sets.title: Arithmetic practice: Class V basics
sets.description: Place value, decimals, fractions, factors and multiples, measurement, perimeter and area, and reading data — the arithmetic topics listed in the JNVST prospectus.

questions.prompt: What is the place value of 7 in 4,73,215?
questions.explanation: In 4,73,215 the 7 is in the ten-thousands place, so its place value is 7 × 10,000 = 70,000.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest number?
questions.explanation: Compare the tenths digit first: 0.054 has 0 tenths, the others have 4 or 5. So 0.054 is the smallest.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24 … The first one that 6 also divides is 24.

questions.prompt: A garden is a rectangle 12 m long and 8 m wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth) = 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m. (96 would be the area in square metres.)

questions.prompt: What is the area of a square with sides of 9 cm?
questions.explanation: Area of a square = side × side = 9 × 9 = 81 sq cm.

questions.prompt: A pencil costs ₹6. How much do 15 pencils cost?
How many minutes are there in 2 hours 15 minutes?
questions.explanation: 2 hours = 120 minutes; 120 + 15 = 135 minutes.

questions.prompt: Which number is a factor of 36 but not a factor of 24?
questions.explanation: 36 ÷ 9 = 4, but 24 ÷ 9 is not a whole number. 6, 12 and 4 divide both 36 and 24.

questions.prompt: What is 1/3 of 45 added to 1/5 of 45?
Books read in a month: Asha 12, Ravi 8, Meena 15, Kabir 10. How many more books did Meena read than Ravi?
questions.explanation: Meena read 15 and Ravi read 8; 15 − 8 = 7.

sets.title: Reading comprehension: two passages
sets.description: Two short passages with five questions each, like the JNVST Language Test, which has four passages with five questions each.

passages.title: The village library
passages.text: Every Sunday morning, Leela walked to the small library near the village pond. The library had only one room, but its shelves were full of books donated by the people of the village. Mr. Das, a retired teacher, looked after it without taking any money. He had one rule: every child who borrowed a book had to tell him one new thing they had learnt from it. Leela liked this rule. Last week she had borrowed a book about birds and told Mr. Das that the tailorbird stitches leaves together to make its nest. This Sunday she wanted a book about the stars.

passages.title: Saving rainwater
passages.text: In many parts of India, rain falls only for a few months of the year. People in dry areas have found clever ways to save rainwater. In some villages of Rajasthan, families build covered underground tanks called tankas. Rainwater from the roof or the courtyard flows into the tank and is used for drinking during the dry months. Keeping the tank covered stops dust from getting in and keeps the water clean. Today, many schools and buildings in cities also collect rainwater from their roofs. This is called rooftop rainwater harvesting.

sets.title: Reasoning warm-up (text-based)
sets.description: Series, odd-one-out, analogies, coding, order and direction questions to build reasoning speed. The real JNVST Mental Ability Test uses figures: practise those with our figure reasoning set and the official sample questions in the prospectus.

questions.prompt: What comes next? 2, 5, 8, 11, ?
questions.explanation: Add 3 each time: 11 + 3 = 14.

questions.prompt: What comes next? 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
questions.explanation: Each number is doubled: 24 × 2 = 48.

questions.prompt: Which one is different from the others?
questions.explanation: A potato is a vegetable; the others are fruits.

questions.prompt: Pen is to write as knife is to ?
questions.explanation: A pen is used to write; a knife is used to cut.

questions.prompt: If CAT is written as DBU, how is DOG written?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one step forward: D→E, O→P, G→H, so DOG becomes EPH.

questions.prompt: What comes next? A, C, E, G, ?
questions.explanation: Skip one letter each time: A (B) C (D) E (F) G (H) I.

questions.prompt: Ravi is taller than Sonu. Sonu is taller than Amit. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: Ravi > Sonu > Amit in height, so Amit is the shortest.

questions.prompt: Meera is facing north. She turns to her right. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation: When you face north, your right hand points east.

questions.prompt: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be 10 days from today?
questions.explanation: After 7 days it is Wednesday again; 3 more days is Saturday.

questions.prompt: Which capital letter looks exactly the same in a mirror held beside it?
questions.explanation: A is the same on its left and right halves, so its mirror image looks the same. F, G and R face the other way in a mirror.

sets.title: AISSEE Class VI Mathematics practice
sets.description: Mathematics carries 150 of the 300 marks in AISSEE Class VI. These questions cover topics from the official syllabus: HCF and LCM, percentage, ratio, profit and loss, simple interest, Roman numerals, angles, volume, average and speed.

questions.prompt: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 18 and 24?
questions.explanation: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The highest common one is 6.

questions.prompt: What is the LCM of 4, 6 and 10?
What is 25% of 360?
questions.explanation: 25% is one quarter: 360 ÷ 4 = 90.

questions.prompt: What is the ratio of 40 minutes to 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Use the same unit: 2 hours = 120 minutes. 40 : 120 = 1 : 3.

questions.prompt: A shopkeeper buys a toy for ₹250 and sells it for ₹300. What is the profit per cent?
questions.explanation: Profit = ₹50. Profit % = 50 ÷ 250 × 100 = 20%. (Profit per cent is always on the cost price.)

questions.prompt: What is the simple interest on ₹2,000 at 5% per year for 3 years?
What number does XLIV stand for?
What is the supplement of an angle of 65°?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add up to 180°: 180° − 65° = 115°. (25° would be the complement.)

questions.prompt: What is the volume of a cube with edges of 4 cm?
questions.explanation: Volume of a cube = edge × edge × edge = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cubic cm.

questions.prompt: What is the average of 12, 15, 18 and 23?
A train travels 180 km in 3 hours at a steady speed. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 51 = 3 × 17, 57 = 3 × 19 and 91 = 7 × 13. 59 has no factors other than 1 and itself.

questions.prompt: Write 0.75 as a fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.explanation: 0.75 = 75/100; dividing both by 25 gives 3/4.

questions.prompt: 5 km 40 m = ? m
If 8 pens cost ₹96, how much do 5 pens cost?
questions.explanation: One pen costs 96 ÷ 8 = ₹12, so 5 pens cost 5 × 12 = ₹60.

sets.title: JNV Class IX entry: Mathematics and Science practice
sets.description: Mathematics and General Science together carry 70 of the 100 marks in the Class IX lateral entry test. These questions follow chapters listed in the NVS prospectus syllabus.

questions.prompt: What is the square root of 1,296?
questions.explanation: 36 × 36 = 1,296. (It ends in 6, so the root ends in 4 or 6; 35² = 1,225 is too small and 36² fits.)

questions.prompt: What is the cube of 7?
Solve: 3x + 5 = 20
Expand (x + 3)²
questions.explanation: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², so (x + 3)² = x² + 2·x·3 + 9 = x² + 6x + 9.
When multiplying powers of the same base, add the exponents: 2⁵⁺³ = 2⁸.

questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has all four sides equal and every angle equal to 90°. What is it?
questions.explanation: Equal sides with right angles make a square. A rhombus has equal sides but its angles need not be 90°; a rectangle has right angles but its sides need not all be equal.

questions.prompt: What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 10% per year, compounded annually?
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)
Which microorganism turns milk into curd?
questions.explanation: Lactobacillus bacteria multiply in milk and turn it into curd. Yeast is used in baking, Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in root nodules, and Penicillium gives penicillin.

questions.prompt: Which gas is needed for combustion (burning)?
questions.explanation: Combustion needs a fuel, heat and oxygen (air). Carbon dioxide is used in fire extinguishers because it cuts off oxygen.

questions.prompt: Sound cannot travel through which of these?
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel. A vacuum has no medium.

questions.prompt: Which of these liquids conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: Lemon juice is acidic and conducts electricity. Distilled water, oil and kerosene are poor conductors.

questions.prompt: A ray of light falls on a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence: 30°.

questions.prompt: Which of these reduces friction?
options: Using a lubricant such as oil
questions.explanation: Lubricants form a thin layer between surfaces so they slide more easily. The other options increase friction.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Coal formed over millions of years from buried plant remains, so it is a fossil fuel. Wood, cow-dung cake and biogas are renewable.

sets.title: AISSEE Class VI: General Knowledge quiz 1
sets.description: National symbols, the Earth and solar system, the human body, food, farming, health and culture — the General Knowledge areas of the AISSEE Class VI syllabus.

questions.prompt: What is the national animal of India?
questions.explanation: The tiger (Bengal tiger) is the national animal of India. The peacock is the national bird.

questions.prompt: Who wrote 'Jana Gana Mana', India's national anthem?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram', the national song.

questions.prompt: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra on the national flag have?
questions.explanation: The navy-blue Ashoka Chakra in the centre of the flag has 24 spokes.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet — more than 11 times as wide as the Earth.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain peak in the world?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, is the highest peak above sea level. K2 is second and Kangchenjunga third.

questions.prompt: Water vapour in the air cools and turns into tiny droplets that form clouds. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Condensation is vapour turning back into liquid. Evaporation is the opposite; precipitation is rain or snow falling; transpiration is water given off by plants.

questions.prompt: India's three armed forces are the Army, the Navy and the ___.
questions.explanation: The Indian Army, Navy and Air Force are the three services of the armed forces. The BSF, CRPF and Assam Rifles are central armed police forces.

questions.prompt: In a hockey match, how many players of one team are on the field at a time?
questions.explanation: Each field-hockey team has 11 players on the field, including the goalkeeper.

questions.prompt: In which city is the headquarters of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York. Geneva has the UN's European office, but the main headquarters is in New York.

questions.prompt: In which organ is most of the digestion and absorption of food completed?
questions.explanation: Digestion is completed in the small intestine, and digested food is absorbed through its walls into the blood. The large intestine mainly absorbs water.

questions.prompt: Why is salt added to pickles?
options: To stop microbes from growing, so the pickle lasts longer
questions.explanation: Salt draws water out of food and microbes, so they cannot grow. Salt, oil and sugar are common preservatives.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Sunlight will not run out, so solar energy is renewable. Coal, petrol and natural gas are fossil fuels that take millions of years to form.

questions.prompt: Malaria is spread by the bite of which insect?
questions.explanation: The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. Removing stagnant water, where mosquitoes breed, helps prevent it.

questions.prompt: Kathakali is a classical dance form of which state?
questions.explanation: Kathakali comes from Kerala. Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu, Odissi from Odisha and Manipuri from Manipur.

questions.prompt: An earthquake under the sea can cause huge waves that strike the coast. What are these waves called?
questions.explanation: A tsunami is a series of huge waves caused by an undersea earthquake or volcano. A cyclone is a storm; an avalanche is a fall of snow.

questions.prompt: Rice is mainly grown in India as which kind of crop, sown with the start of the monsoon?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops such as rice, maize and cotton are sown with the monsoon (June–July). Rabi crops such as wheat are sown in winter.

questions.prompt: Which part of a plant absorbs water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil; the stem carries them up to the leaves.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to measure body temperature?
questions.explanation: A clinical thermometer measures body temperature. A barometer measures air pressure, a speedometer speed, and a stethoscope is used to listen to the heart and lungs.

sets.title: AISSEE Class VI: Language (English) quiz 1
sets.description: A short passage, then vocabulary, idioms, parts of speech, articles, tenses, question tags, plurals, collective nouns and spelling — the Language areas of the AISSEE Class VI syllabus.

passages.title: The puppy behind the bricks
passages.text: Rohan was walking home from school when he heard a soft whimpering sound coming from behind a pile of bricks. He looked closely and found a small brown puppy with a white patch over one eye. The puppy was shivering, and one of its paws was cut. Rohan wrapped it in his handkerchief and carried it home. His mother washed the wound, and his sister brought a bowl of warm milk. The next morning Rohan put up notices near the market, but no one came to claim the puppy. After a week, his parents agreed that it could stay. Rohan named it Patch, after the white mark on its face.

questions.prompt: Where did Rohan find the puppy?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says the sound came from behind a pile of bricks.

questions.prompt: Why did Rohan name the puppy Patch?
options: Because of the white mark over its eye
Its paw had a patch of cloth on it
It was found on a patch of grass
questions.explanation: The last sentence says he named it Patch after the white mark on its face.

questions.prompt: What did Rohan do to find the puppy's owner?
options: He put up notices near the market
He took it to the police station
He searched the streets every evening
questions.explanation: The next morning Rohan put up notices near the market.

questions.prompt: In the passage, 'whimpering' means:
questions.explanation: To whimper is to make low, weak crying sounds, as a hurt or frightened animal does.

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'enormous'.
questions.explanation: Enormous means very large — huge. Tiny is its opposite.

questions.prompt: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'ancient'.
questions.explanation: Ancient means very old; its opposite is modern.

questions.prompt: 'A piece of cake' means something that is:
questions.explanation: The idiom 'a piece of cake' describes a task that is very easy.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'She sings beautifully', the word 'beautifully' is:
questions.explanation: 'Beautifully' tells us how she sings, so it describes the verb — it is an adverb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The cat is hiding ___ the table.
questions.explanation: 'Under' tells us where the cat is. 'At', 'of' and 'since' do not fit here.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: She is ___ honest girl.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: Yesterday, we ___ to the zoo.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' shows the past, so the simple past 'went' is correct.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: You are coming to the party, ___?
questions.explanation: A positive sentence with 'you are' takes the negative tag 'aren't you?'.

questions.prompt: What is the plural of 'child'?
questions.explanation: 'Child' has an irregular plural: 'children'.

questions.prompt: Choose the collective noun: a ___ of cows.
questions.explanation: We say a herd of cows (also of elephants or deer). A pride is of lions and a swarm of bees.

questions.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly?
questions.explanation: Remember 'i before e, except after c': re-c-ei-ve.

questions.prompt: What is the feminine of 'lion'?
questions.explanation: The female lion is a lioness. A tigress is a female tiger, a mare a female horse and a doe a female deer.

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'light'?
questions.explanation: 'Kite' ends with the same sound as 'light' (-ite).

sets.title: AISSEE Class VI: Intelligence quiz 1
sets.description: Analogies, classification, number and letter series, family relations, coding, ranking, directions and simple puzzles — the Intelligence areas of the AISSEE Class VI syllabus.

questions.prompt: Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?

questions.explanation: Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai are Indian cities; Nepal is a country.

questions.explanation: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) and the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W).

questions.explanation: Neha's mother's only son is Neha's brother. The boy is her brother's son, so he is Neha's nephew.

questions.explanation: Add the two positions and subtract 1, because Asha is counted twice: 7 + 10 − 1 = 16.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number: 3, 9, 27, ?, 243
questions.explanation: Each number is 3 times the one before: 27 × 3 = 81, and 81 × 3 = 243.

questions.prompt: A clock shows exactly 3 o'clock. What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand?
questions.explanation: The minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand at 3: three of the twelve 30° gaps, so 3 × 30° = 90°.

questions.prompt: Ravi walks 5 m north, turns right and walks 3 m, then turns right again and walks 5 m. How far is he from where he started?
questions.explanation: North 5 m, east 3 m, then south 5 m brings him back level with the start but 3 m to the east.

questions.prompt: Find the rule and the missing number: 5 → 26, 6 → 37, 7 → ?
questions.explanation: Each number is squared and 1 is added: 5 × 5 + 1 = 26, 6 × 6 + 1 = 37, so 7 × 7 + 1 = 50.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, a straight line is drawn from A to a point D on side BC. How many triangles are there in the figure?
questions.explanation: There are triangles ABD and ADC, and the whole triangle ABC: 3 in all.

questions.prompt: Which is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: A square, a rectangle and a rhombus each have four sides; a triangle has three.

sets.title: AISSEE Class IX: Mathematics quiz 1
sets.description: Rational numbers, linear equations, percentages and discounts, exponents, factorisation, identities, polygons, mensuration, proportion, cube roots, probability and averages — Class VIII mathematics for Class IX entry.

questions.prompt: What is the additive inverse of −3/7?
questions.explanation: A number plus its additive inverse is 0: −3/7 + 3/7 = 0.

questions.prompt: What is the multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of −5/8?
questions.explanation: A number times its reciprocal is 1: (−5/8) × (−8/5) = 1. The sign stays the same.

questions.prompt: If 2(x − 3) = x + 4, what is x?
A price rises from ₹400 to ₹460. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: Increase = ₹60. Percentage increase = 60 ÷ 400 × 100 = 15%. (It is always worked out on the original amount.)

questions.prompt: A shirt marked ₹1,200 is sold at a 15% discount. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Discount = 15% of 1,200 = ₹180. Selling price = 1,200 − 180 = ₹1,020.

questions.prompt: Write 0.000035 in standard form.
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point 5 places to the right to get 3.5, so 0.000035 = 3.5 × 10⁻⁵.

questions.prompt: Factorise x² − 9.
questions.explanation: x² − 9 = x² − 3², and a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b), so it is (x − 3)(x + 3).

questions.prompt: Using an identity, 102 × 98 = ?
What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°. For a hexagon, n = 6: 4 × 180° = 720°.

questions.prompt: A trapezium has parallel sides of 10 cm and 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height = ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 sq cm.

questions.prompt: 12 workers can build a wall in 10 days. How many days will 15 workers take, working at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The work is 12 × 10 = 120 worker-days. With 15 workers: 120 ÷ 15 = 8 days. More workers, fewer days.

questions.prompt: What is the cube root of 2,744?
A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting an even number?
questions.explanation: Three of the six faces (2, 4, 6) are even: 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.prompt: The mean of 5 numbers is 18. If the number 10 is removed, what is the mean of the remaining four?
questions.explanation: The total is 5 × 18 = 90. Without 10 it is 80, and 80 ÷ 4 = 20.

questions.prompt: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle are 6 cm and 8 cm. How long is the longest side?
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, and √100 = 10 cm.

questions.prompt: The sum of three consecutive whole numbers is 72. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation: Let them be n, n + 1, n + 2: 3n + 3 = 72, so n = 23. The numbers are 23, 24 and 25.

questions.prompt: How many cubes with 2 cm edges fit exactly into a cuboid 6 cm × 4 cm × 2 cm?
questions.explanation: Along the edges: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 4 ÷ 2 = 2, 2 ÷ 2 = 1, so 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 cubes. (Or: 48 cubic cm ÷ 8 cubic cm = 6.)

sets.title: AISSEE Class IX: English quiz 1
sets.description: A factual passage, then reported speech, active and passive voice, agreement, synonyms and antonyms, idioms, conjunctions, spelling, tenses and prepositions — for Class IX entry, where the paper is in English only.

passages.title: The Great Indian Bustard
passages.text: The Great Indian Bustard is one of the heaviest flying birds in the world. It lives in dry grasslands, mostly in Rajasthan and Gujarat. Once found across much of western and central India, it is now critically endangered, and only a small number survive in the wild. Many birds have died after flying into overhead power lines, which they find hard to see because their eyes look out to the sides rather than straight ahead. Conservationists are now asking for power lines to be moved underground in the areas where the birds live, and are breeding the birds in special centres, hoping to return them to the wild one day.

questions.prompt: Where does the Great Indian Bustard mainly live today?
options: Dry grasslands, mostly in Rajasthan and Gujarat
questions.explanation: The passage says it lives in dry grasslands, mostly in Rajasthan and Gujarat.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why do the birds fly into power lines?
options: The lines are built on their nests
Their eyes look out to the sides, so wires ahead are hard to see
They are attracted to the wires
questions.explanation: The passage explains that the lines are hard to see because the birds' eyes look out to the sides rather than straight ahead.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means 'in danger of dying out completely'?
questions.explanation: 'Critically endangered' means at very high risk of dying out in the wild.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To compare the birds of India
To tell the story of a bird-watcher
To explain why a bird is in danger and what is being done to save it
To describe how power lines are built
questions.explanation: The passage describes the bird, why its numbers have fallen, and the steps being taken to protect it.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct reported form: She said, "I am tired."
options: She said that I am tired.
She said that she is being tired.
She said that she was tired.
She says that she was tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech after 'said', 'I' becomes 'she' and 'am' moves back to 'was'.

questions.prompt: Choose the passive form of: The chef cooked the meal.
options: The meal is cooked by the chef.
The meal was cooked by the chef.
The chef was cooked by the meal.
The meal has cooked the chef.
questions.explanation: The object 'the meal' becomes the subject, and the simple past 'cooked' becomes 'was cooked'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ present.
questions.explanation: With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'The students' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'diligent'.
questions.explanation: A diligent person works carefully and steadily — hard-working. Lazy and careless are its opposites.

questions.prompt: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'scarce'.
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply; plentiful means there is a lot. 'Rare' is close in meaning to scarce.

questions.prompt: 'To burn the midnight oil' means:
options: To work or study late into the night
questions.explanation: The idiom comes from working by lamplight late at night: it means studying or working late.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: He was ill, ___ he went to school.
questions.explanation: The two ideas contrast (ill, yet he went), so 'but' is correct.

questions.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Accommodation' has a double c and a double m.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues now takes the present perfect ('has lived'). 'Since' is used with a point in time such as 2015; 'for' with a length of time.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: He is good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: We say 'good at' a subject or activity.

sets.title: AISSEE Class IX: General Science quiz 1
sets.description: Crops, cells, reproduction, force and pressure, metals, plastics, pollution, stars, the eye, hormones, electroplating, lightning, sound, microbes and conservation — Class VIII science for Class IX entry.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a rabi crop?
questions.explanation: Rabi crops such as wheat, gram and mustard are sown in winter. Paddy, maize and cotton are kharif (monsoon) crops.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell controls its activities?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains the genetic material and controls the activities of the cell.

questions.prompt: Which of these is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts, which carry out photosynthesis, are found in plant cells. Both kinds of cell have a nucleus, mitochondria and a cell membrane.

questions.prompt: In which of these animals does fertilisation take place outside the body?
questions.explanation: Frogs lay eggs in water, where they are fertilised — external fertilisation. In hens, cows and humans it happens inside the body.

questions.prompt: Pressure is:
questions.explanation: Pressure = force ÷ area. That is why a sharp knife (small area) cuts more easily than a blunt one.

questions.prompt: Which metal is stored in kerosene because it reacts strongly with air and water?
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts so strongly with oxygen and water that it can catch fire, so it is kept under kerosene.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a thermosetting plastic that does not soften when heated?
questions.explanation: Bakelite sets hard once moulded and does not soften on heating, so it is used for switches and pan handles. Polythene and PVC are thermoplastics; nylon is a synthetic fibre.

questions.prompt: Which gas released by burning fuels is mainly responsible for the greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere. Burning coal, petrol and wood adds more of it to the air.

questions.prompt: Which star is nearest to the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, and the nearest one to us. Proxima Centauri is the nearest star after the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which coloured part of the eye controls the size of the pupil?
questions.explanation: The iris is the coloured part; it makes the pupil smaller in bright light and larger in dim light.

questions.prompt: Which gland releases the hormone insulin?
questions.explanation: The pancreas releases insulin, which controls the level of sugar in the blood. The thyroid releases thyroxine.

questions.prompt: What is it called when electricity is used to deposit a thin layer of one metal on another?
questions.explanation: In electroplating, a current passed through a solution coats an object with a metal such as chromium or silver.

questions.prompt: Lightning is caused by:
options: The discharge of electric charges built up in clouds
Gases burning high in the sky
questions.explanation: Charges build up in clouds; when they become large, they discharge as a giant spark — lightning. Thunder is the sound it makes.

questions.prompt: In which unit is the frequency of a sound measured?
questions.explanation: Frequency (vibrations per second) is measured in hertz (Hz). Loudness is measured in decibels.

questions.prompt: Which of these diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Polio is caused by a virus. Typhoid, cholera and tuberculosis are caused by bacteria.

questions.prompt: An area where wild animals are protected in their natural habitat and hunting is banned is called a:
questions.explanation: A wildlife sanctuary protects animals in their natural surroundings. A zoo keeps animals in enclosures.

sets.title: AISSEE Class IX: Social Science quiz 1
sets.description: Modern Indian history, the Constitution and Parliament, rivers, soils, resources, the Tropic of Cancer, industries and farming — Class VIII social science for Class IX entry.

questions.prompt: On 10 May 1857, the revolt of soldiers began at which place?
questions.explanation: The revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857; the soldiers then marched to Delhi.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 in Bombay (now Mumbai).

questions.prompt: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the East India Company and:
questions.explanation: At Plassey in 1757, Robert Clive's forces defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal.

questions.prompt: Under whose leadership was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched in 1920?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920.

questions.prompt: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, now celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution. Dr Rajendra Prasad was President of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.prompt: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha for their knowledge of fields such as art, literature, science and social service.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a Fundamental Right in the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: The Right to Equality is a Fundamental Right. The Right to Property was removed from the Fundamental Rights in 1978 and is now a legal right.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest river flowing in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga, about 2,500 km long, is the longest river in India. The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India.

questions.prompt: Black soil is best suited for growing which crop?
questions.explanation: Black soil holds moisture well and is ideal for cotton, which is why it is also called black cotton soil.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a non-renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Petroleum takes millions of years to form and will run out; sun and wind are renewable.

questions.prompt: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of these states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram — not Bihar.

questions.prompt: Jute mills are concentrated mainly in which state?
questions.explanation: Most jute mills are along the Hooghly river in West Bengal, close to where jute is grown.

questions.prompt: Which layer of the Earth do we live on?
questions.explanation: We live on the crust, the thin outermost layer. Below it are the mantle and the core.

questions.prompt: Shifting cultivation is called 'jhum' in which part of India?
questions.explanation: In the north-eastern states, shifting cultivation — clearing a patch of forest, farming it, then moving on — is known as jhum.

sets.title: AISSEE Class IX: Intelligence quiz 1
sets.description: Series, coding, analogies, family relations, ranking, clocks, statements and conclusions, calendars and directions — reasoning for Class IX entry.

questions.prompt: What comes next? 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ?
questions.explanation: Each number is the sum of the two before it: 5 + 8 = 13.

questions.prompt: What comes next? 3, 7, 15, 31, ?
questions.explanation: Each number is doubled and 1 is added: 31 × 2 + 1 = 63.

questions.prompt: If MONKEY is written as XDJMNL, how is TIGER written in the same code?
questions.explanation: The word is written backwards (YEKNOM) and each letter moves one step back (Y→X, E→D, K→J …). TIGER backwards is REGIT, which becomes QDFHS.

questions.prompt: Ornithology : Birds :: Entomology : ?
questions.explanation: Ornithology is the study of birds; entomology is the study of insects.

questions.prompt: A is B's brother. C is A's mother. D is C's father. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation: C is the mother of A and B, and D is C's father, so D is B's grandfather (mother's father).

questions.prompt: In a class of 40 students, Kiran is 12th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation: Rank from the bottom = total − rank from the top + 1 = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29.

questions.prompt: How many times do the hour and minute hands of a clock point in exactly the same direction in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: The minute hand laps the hour hand 11 times in 12 hours (the overlap between 11 and 1 o'clock happens only once, at 12).

questions.prompt: Statements: All pens are books. All books are tables. Which conclusion must be true?
questions.explanation: Every pen is a book and every book is a table, so every pen is a table. The other conclusions do not follow from the statements.

questions.prompt: If 1 January of a non-leap year is a Monday, what day is 1 January of the next year?
questions.explanation: A non-leap year has 365 days = 52 weeks and 1 day, so the day moves on by one: Tuesday.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number: 8, 27, 64, ?, 216
questions.explanation: These are cubes: 2³, 3³, 4³, 5³ = 125, 6³.

questions.prompt: Arun is facing south. He turns 90° clockwise and then turns 180°. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: From south, 90° clockwise faces west; turning 180° from west faces east.

questions.prompt: Which number is the odd one out? 121, 169, 196, 210
questions.explanation: 121 = 11², 169 = 13² and 196 = 14² are perfect squares; 210 is not.

sets.title: JNVST-style: Environmental Studies quiz 1
sets.description: Plants, animals, the human body, food, water, materials, directions, our past and a passage with questions — like the Environmental Studies part of the JNVST paper.

passages.title: The Chipko movement
passages.text: The Chipko movement began in the early 1970s in the hills of what is now Uttarakhand. When contractors came to cut down the trees near their villages, the villagers went into the forest and hugged the trees so that they could not be felled. At Reni village, women led by Gaura Devi stood guard over the trees in this way. The word chipko means "to stick" or "to hug". The protest spread to many villages and made people across India think about why forests matter: they hold the soil together, keep springs flowing and give fuel, fodder and food.

questions.prompt: Which of these animals is a herbivore (eats only plants)?
questions.explanation: A deer eats grass and leaves. Lions and eagles eat other animals, and frogs eat insects.

questions.prompt: Which organs help us to breathe?
questions.explanation: We breathe in air through the nose into the lungs, where oxygen passes into the blood.

questions.prompt: Bats can fly in the dark without bumping into things because they:
options: listen to the echoes of the sounds they make
questions.explanation: Bats make high-pitched sounds and listen to the echoes that bounce back from objects. This is called echolocation.

questions.prompt: Which of these rots (decomposes) fastest in soil?
questions.explanation: Vegetable peels are broken down by microbes in a few weeks and can become compost. Plastic, glass and aluminium last for many years.

questions.prompt: At what temperature does pure water boil at sea level?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level (that is 212 °F on the Fahrenheit scale). It freezes at 0 °C.

questions.prompt: In which direction does the Sun rise?
questions.explanation: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

questions.prompt: What do we call people who dig up and study old things such as coins, tools and buildings to learn about the past?
questions.explanation: Archaeologists study remains of the past. Astronomers study stars, botanists plants and geologists rocks.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest desert in India?
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert is mostly in Rajasthan. The Sahara and Kalahari are in Africa, and the Gobi is in China and Mongolia.

questions.prompt: Snake-boat races (vallam kali) are famous in which state?
questions.explanation: Snake-boat races are held on the backwaters of Kerala, especially around the Onam festival.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a sign that the body has lost too much water (dehydration)?
questions.explanation: With dehydration a person feels thirsty and weak, with a dry mouth. Drinking water, or ORS in case of diarrhoea, helps.

questions.prompt: Which of these helps a camel live in the hot desert?
options: Its thick fur keeps it cool in water
It stores water in its hump
Its long legs keep its body away from the hot sand
It drinks water only once a year
questions.explanation: A camel's long legs keep its body away from the hot sand. Its hump stores fat, not water — a common mistake.

questions.prompt: What does a seed need to germinate (start to grow)?
questions.explanation: A seed needs water, air and a suitable temperature to germinate. Sunlight is needed later, once green leaves appear.

questions.prompt: What did the villagers do to save the trees?
options: They wrote letters to the king
questions.explanation: The passage says they went into the forest and hugged the trees so that they could not be felled.

questions.prompt: What does the word 'chipko' mean?
questions.explanation: The passage says chipko means "to stick" or "to hug".

questions.prompt: In which present-day state did the movement begin?
questions.explanation: It began in the hills of what is now Uttarakhand.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how do forests help people?
questions.explanation: The last sentence lists ways forests help: they hold the soil together, keep springs flowing and give fuel, fodder and food.

sets.title: JNVST-style: Arithmetic quiz 2
sets.description: Large numbers, ordering fractions, simplification, capacity, perimeter, angles, fractions of quantities, divisibility, time, rounding, pictographs, area and money.

questions.prompt: Which number is 1,000 more than 9,99,500?
Arrange in ascending order (smallest first): 3/5, 1/2, 7/10
Simplify: 48 ÷ 6 + 4 × 3 − 5
questions.explanation: Divide and multiply first: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 4 × 3 = 12. Then 8 + 12 − 5 = 15.

questions.prompt: A bottle holds 2 litres 750 mL. How many millilitres is that?
A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter is the sum of the sides: 7 + 9 + 12 = 28 cm.

questions.prompt: An angle of 120° is:
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is more than 90° and less than 180°.

questions.prompt: A shopkeeper had 450 mangoes and sold 3/5 of them. How many were left?
What is the smallest 4-digit number that is exactly divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: 1,000 ÷ 9 leaves remainder 1, so add 8: 1,008 = 9 × 112. (1,017 is also divisible by 9 but is larger.)

questions.prompt: Priya started her homework at 4:45 p.m. and finished at 6:10 p.m. How long did she work?
questions.explanation: From 4:45 to 5:45 is 1 hour; from 5:45 to 6:10 is 25 minutes. Total: 1 hour 25 minutes.

questions.prompt: Round 4,867 to the nearest hundred.
questions.explanation: The tens digit is 6 (5 or more), so round up: 4,867 → 4,900.

questions.prompt: In a pictograph, one picture of a book stands for 5 students. Class 5A has 7 pictures. How many students is that?
questions.explanation: 7 pictures × 5 students = 35 students.

questions.prompt: The area of a square is 64 sq cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Side × side = 64, so the side is 8 cm. Perimeter = 4 × 8 = 32 cm.

questions.prompt: Which number is a multiple of both 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: 36 = 4 × 9 = 6 × 6. 18 is not a multiple of 4, and 20 and 26 are not multiples of 6.

questions.prompt: ₹500 is shared equally among 4 children. How much does each child get?
questions.explanation: 500 ÷ 4 = 125, so each child gets ₹125.

sets.title: Class X Mathematics: chapter-wise practice
sets.description: Original questions across the Class X mathematics syllabus, from real numbers to probability, in English and Hindi. Check your board's current syllabus for the exact chapter list.

questions.prompt: The HCF of 96 and 404 is 4. What is their LCM?
questions.explanation: HCF × LCM = product of the numbers, so LCM = (96 × 404) ÷ 4 = 38784 ÷ 4 = 9696.

hi.prompt: 96 और 404 का म.स. (HCF) 4 है। इनका ल.स. (LCM) क्या है?

questions.prompt: Which of these numbers is irrational?
questions.explanation: √2 × √8 = √16 = 4, 0.375 = 3/8 and 22/7 are all rational. √5 is irrational, and a rational number plus an irrational number is irrational.

hi.prompt: इनमें से कौन-सी संख्या अपरिमेय है?
hi.explanation: √2 × √8 = √16 = 4, 0.375 = 3/8 और 22/7 सभी परिमेय हैं। √5 अपरिमेय है, और परिमेय तथा अपरिमेय संख्या का योग अपरिमेय होता है।

questions.prompt: For the polynomial 2x² − 8x + 6, what are the sum and the product of its zeros?
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c, sum of zeros = −b/a = 8/2 = 4 and product = c/a = 6/2 = 3.

hi.prompt: बहुपद 2x² − 8x + 6 के शून्यकों का योग और गुणनफल क्या है?
hi.explanation: ax² + bx + c के लिए शून्यकों का योग = −b/a = 8/2 = 4 और गुणनफल = c/a = 6/2 = 3।

questions.prompt: Which quadratic polynomial has zeros 3 and −2?
questions.explanation: Sum of zeros = 3 + (−2) = 1 and product = −6, so the polynomial is x² − (sum)x + product = x² − x − 6.

hi.prompt: किस द्विघात बहुपद के शून्यक 3 और −2 हैं?
hi.explanation: शून्यकों का योग = 3 + (−2) = 1 और गुणनफल = −6, इसलिए बहुपद x² − (योग)x + गुणनफल = x² − x − 6 है।

questions.prompt: For which value of k do 2x + 3y = 7 and 4x + ky = 14 have infinitely many solutions?

questions.prompt: What are the roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0?
questions.explanation: x² − 7x + 12 = (x − 3)(x − 4), so the roots are 3 and 4. Check: 3 + 4 = 7 and 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.prompt: What is the nature of the roots of 2x² − 4x + 3 = 0?

hi.prompt: 2x² − 4x + 3 = 0 के मूलों की प्रकृति क्या है?

questions.prompt: What is the 10th term of the AP 3, 7, 11, …?
What is the sum of the first 20 terms of the AP 2, 5, 8, …?

hi.prompt: समांतर श्रेढ़ी 2, 5, 8, … के पहले 20 पदों का योग क्या है?

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm and AE = 4 cm, what is EC?
questions.explanation: By the basic proportionality theorem AD/DB = AE/EC, so 2/3 = 4/EC and EC = 6 cm.

hi.prompt: त्रिभुज ABC में DE ∥ BC है, जहाँ D भुजा AB पर और E भुजा AC पर है। यदि AD = 2 सेमी, DB = 3 सेमी और AE = 4 सेमी है, तो EC क्या है?
hi.explanation: आधारभूत समानुपातिकता प्रमेय से AD/DB = AE/EC, अतः 2/3 = 4/EC और EC = 6 सेमी।

questions.prompt: The corresponding sides of two similar triangles are in the ratio 3 : 5. What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.explanation: The areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides: 3² : 5² = 9 : 25.

hi.prompt: दो समरूप त्रिभुजों की संगत भुजाओं का अनुपात 3 : 5 है। उनके क्षेत्रफलों का अनुपात क्या है?
hi.explanation: समरूप त्रिभुजों के क्षेत्रफलों का अनुपात संगत भुजाओं के वर्गों के अनुपात के बराबर होता है: 3² : 5² = 9 : 25।

questions.prompt: What is the distance between the points (2, 3) and (8, 11)?
What is the mid-point of the segment joining (−4, 6) and (8, −2)?

hi.prompt: (−4, 6) और (8, −2) को मिलाने वाले रेखाखंड का मध्य-बिंदु क्या है?

questions.prompt: If A is an acute angle and sin A = 3/5, what is tan A?

hi.prompt: यदि A एक न्यून कोण है और sin A = 3/5 है, तो tan A क्या है?

questions.prompt: What is the value of sin² 30° + cos² 60°?
questions.explanation: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2, so the value is 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2.

hi.prompt: sin² 30° + cos² 60° का मान क्या है?

questions.prompt: What is the area of a sector of a circle of radius 14 cm with central angle 90°? (Take π = 22/7.)

hi.prompt: 14 सेमी त्रिज्या वाले वृत्त के उस त्रिज्यखंड का क्षेत्रफल क्या है जिसका केंद्रीय कोण 90° है? (π = 22/7 लीजिए।)

questions.prompt: What is the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7.)

hi.prompt: 7 सेमी त्रिज्या और 10 सेमी ऊँचाई वाले बेलन का आयतन क्या है? (π = 22/7 लीजिए।)

questions.prompt: What is the mean of 4, 8, 6, 10 and 12?
A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: The favourable outcomes are 5 and 6, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3.

hi.prompt: एक न्यायसंगत पासा एक बार फेंका जाता है। 4 से बड़ी संख्या आने की प्रायिकता क्या है?
hi.explanation: अनुकूल परिणाम 5 और 6 हैं, इसलिए प्रायिकता = 2/6 = 1/3।

questions.prompt: A bag has 5 red balls and 3 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is blue?
questions.explanation: There are 8 balls and 3 of them are blue, so the probability is 3/8.

hi.prompt: एक थैले में 5 लाल और 3 नीली गेंदें हैं। एक गेंद यादृच्छया निकाली जाती है। उसके नीली होने की प्रायिकता क्या है?
hi.explanation: कुल 8 गेंदें हैं, जिनमें से 3 नीली हैं, इसलिए प्रायिकता = 3/8।

sets.title: Maths Olympiad practice: Class V
sets.description: Original Olympiad-style questions on number sense, patterns, shapes, measurement and logical thinking, in English and Hindi. Not taken from any Olympiad paper.

questions.prompt: What is the largest 4-digit number that can be made using each of the digits 0, 3, 7 and 5 exactly once?
questions.explanation: Put the digits in decreasing order: 7, 5, 3, 0 gives 7530.

hi.prompt: अंक 0, 3, 7 और 5 को एक-एक बार प्रयोग करके बनने वाली सबसे बड़ी चार अंकों की संख्या कौन-सी है?
hi.explanation: अंकों को घटते क्रम में रखिए: 7, 5, 3, 0 से 7530 बनता है।

questions.prompt: What is the smallest 5-digit number that is divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 9 when the sum of its digits is. 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 8 = 9, and no 5-digit number from 10000 to 10007 has a digit sum of 9.

hi.prompt: 9 से विभाज्य सबसे छोटी पाँच अंकों की संख्या कौन-सी है?
hi.explanation: कोई संख्या 9 से तभी विभाज्य होती है जब उसके अंकों का योग 9 से विभाज्य हो। 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 8 = 9, और 10000 से 10007 तक किसी संख्या के अंकों का योग 9 नहीं है।

questions.prompt: What comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, …?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12: 30 + 12 = 42. (Each term is n × (n + 1).)

questions.prompt: Which number is missing: 1, 4, 9, 16, __, 36?
questions.explanation: These are square numbers: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², 6². The missing one is 5² = 25.

hi.explanation: ये वर्ग संख्याएँ हैं: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², 6²। छूटी हुई संख्या 5² = 25 है।

questions.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explanation: A square has 2 lines of symmetry joining the mid-points of opposite sides and 2 along its diagonals: 4 in all.

hi.prompt: एक वर्ग में कितनी सममिति रेखाएँ होती हैं?
hi.explanation: वर्ग में आमने-सामने की भुजाओं के मध्य-बिंदुओं को मिलाने वाली 2 रेखाएँ और 2 विकर्ण सममिति रेखाएँ हैं: कुल 4।

questions.prompt: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at exactly 3 o'clock?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand at 3. Each hour mark is 30° apart, so the angle is 3 × 30° = 90°.

hi.prompt: ठीक 3 बजे घड़ी की घंटे और मिनट की सुइयों के बीच कितना कोण होता है?
hi.explanation: मिनट की सुई 12 पर और घंटे की सुई 3 पर है। हर घंटे के निशान के बीच 30° होते हैं, इसलिए कोण = 3 × 30° = 90°।

questions.prompt: What is the perimeter of a rectangle that is 12 cm long and 5 cm wide?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth) = 2 × (12 + 5) = 34 cm. (60 is the area in cm².)

hi.prompt: 12 सेमी लंबे और 5 सेमी चौड़े आयत का परिमाप क्या है?

questions.prompt: How many minutes are there in 2½ hours?
questions.explanation: 2 hours = 120 minutes and half an hour = 30 minutes, so 2½ hours = 150 minutes.

hi.prompt: 2½ घंटे में कितने मिनट होते हैं?
hi.explanation: 2 घंटे = 120 मिनट और आधा घंटा = 30 मिनट, इसलिए 2½ घंटे = 150 मिनट।

questions.prompt: If today is Wednesday, what day of the week will it be 10 days from today?
questions.explanation: After 7 days it is Wednesday again; 3 more days (Thursday, Friday, Saturday) make it Saturday.

hi.prompt: यदि आज बुधवार है, तो आज से 10 दिन बाद कौन-सा दिन होगा?
hi.explanation: 7 दिन बाद फिर बुधवार होगा; उसके 3 दिन बाद (गुरुवार, शुक्रवार, शनिवार) शनिवार होगा।

questions.prompt: What is the sum of all the odd numbers from 1 to 19?
questions.explanation: There are 10 odd numbers from 1 to 19, and the sum of the first n odd numbers is n × n: 10 × 10 = 100.

hi.prompt: 1 से 19 तक की सभी विषम संख्याओं का योग क्या है?
hi.explanation: 1 से 19 तक 10 विषम संख्याएँ हैं, और पहली n विषम संख्याओं का योग n × n होता है: 10 × 10 = 100।

questions.prompt: What is 3/4 of 120?
Ravi is older than Sita. Sita is older than Mohan. Who is the youngest?
questions.explanation: Ravi > Sita > Mohan in age, so Mohan is the youngest.

hi.prompt: रवि, सीता से बड़ा है। सीता, मोहन से बड़ी है। सबसे छोटा कौन है?
hi.explanation: आयु में रवि > सीता > मोहन, इसलिए मोहन सबसे छोटा है।

questions.prompt: A pen costs ₹15 and a notebook costs ₹35. What do 3 pens and 2 notebooks cost?

hi.prompt: एक कलम ₹15 की और एक कॉपी ₹35 की है। 3 कलम और 2 कॉपियों का मूल्य क्या होगा?

questions.prompt: A square is divided by drawing both of its diagonals. How many triangles of any size are there in the figure?
questions.explanation: The diagonals make 4 small triangles. Each diagonal also cuts the square into 2 larger triangles, adding 4 more: 4 + 4 = 8.

hi.prompt: एक वर्ग में उसके दोनों विकर्ण खींचे जाते हैं। आकृति में किसी भी आकार के कुल कितने त्रिभुज हैं?
hi.explanation: विकर्ण 4 छोटे त्रिभुज बनाते हैं। हर विकर्ण वर्ग को 2 बड़े त्रिभुजों में भी बाँटता है, यानी 4 और: 4 + 4 = 8।

questions.prompt: Which of these is a factor of 84 but not a factor of 36?
questions.explanation: 84 = 7 × 12, so 7 is a factor of 84, but 36 ÷ 7 is not a whole number. 6 and 12 divide both numbers; 9 divides 36 but not 84.

hi.prompt: इनमें से कौन-सी संख्या 84 का गुणनखंड है, पर 36 का नहीं?
hi.explanation: 84 = 7 × 12, इसलिए 7, 84 का गुणनखंड है, पर 36 ÷ 7 पूर्ण संख्या नहीं है। 6 और 12 दोनों को विभाजित करते हैं; 9, 36 को विभाजित करता है पर 84 को नहीं।

sets.title: Class VIII Science: topic-wise practice
sets.description: Original questions on topics commonly taught in Class VIII science: microorganisms, combustion, force and pressure, friction, sound, light and more.

questions.prompt: Which microorganism helps turn milk into curd?
questions.explanation: Lactobacillus bacteria multiply in milk and turn it into curd.

questions.prompt: Which gas, produced by yeast, makes bread dough rise?
questions.explanation: Yeast respires and releases carbon dioxide; the gas bubbles make the dough rise.

questions.prompt: Leguminous plants such as peas and beans add nitrogen to the soil because their root nodules contain:
questions.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria living in the root nodules of legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen into compounds plants can use.

questions.prompt: Which zone of a candle flame is the hottest?
questions.explanation: In the outermost zone the wax vapour burns completely, so it is the hottest part of the flame.

questions.prompt: Why is water not used to put out a fire in electrical equipment?
options: Water conducts electricity and can cause an electric shock
Water makes the fire spread faster
questions.explanation: Water conducts electricity, so using it on an electrical fire can give the person a shock. The power is switched off and a suitable extinguisher is used.

questions.prompt: A force of 100 N acts evenly on an area of 2 m². What is the pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force ÷ area = 100 N ÷ 2 m² = 50 N/m² = 50 pascal.

questions.prompt: Which of these reduces friction?
questions.explanation: Ball bearings replace sliding with rolling, which reduces friction. The other three increase grip.

questions.prompt: Through which of these can sound NOT travel?
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel; it cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.prompt: An object makes 500 vibrations in 2 seconds. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency = vibrations per second = 500 ÷ 2 = 250 hertz.

questions.prompt: A ray of light falls on a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence: 35°.

questions.prompt: Which of these liquids conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: Lemon juice contains acids that form ions, so it conducts. Distilled water, vegetable oil and kerosene are poor conductors.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Natural gas formed over millions of years from buried remains of living things, so it is a fossil fuel. The others come from recently living material.

questions.prompt: Which instrument records the waves produced by an earthquake?
questions.explanation: A seismograph records seismic waves. A barometer measures air pressure and an anemometer wind speed.

questions.prompt: Which hormone is produced by the thyroid gland?
questions.explanation: The thyroid makes thyroxine. Insulin comes from the pancreas, adrenaline from the adrenal glands and testosterone from the testes.

questions.prompt: Frogs lay eggs that develop outside the body. Such animals are called:
questions.explanation: Animals that lay eggs are oviparous; animals that give birth to young ones are viviparous.

questions.prompt: Which of these keeps animals in captivity, outside their natural habitat?
questions.explanation: A zoo keeps animals in enclosures. Sanctuaries, national parks and biosphere reserves protect animals in their natural habitat.

sets.title: Aptitude and reasoning mock: competitive exams
sets.description: An original 15-minute mock on quantitative aptitude and reasoning, the kind of questions common in SSC, banking and railway exams, in English and Hindi. Practice marking here is +1 for a correct answer and −0.25 for a wrong one; each exam publishes its own scheme.

questions.prompt: What is 25% of 480?
questions.explanation: 25% is one quarter, and 480 ÷ 4 = 120.

questions.prompt: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹800 and sells it for ₹920. What is the profit percent?

hi.prompt: एक दुकानदार एक वस्तु ₹800 में खरीदकर ₹920 में बेचता है। लाभ प्रतिशत क्या है?

questions.prompt: What is the average of the first 10 natural numbers?

hi.prompt: पहली 10 प्राकृत संख्याओं का औसत क्या है?

questions.prompt: A car travels at 60 km/h for 2 hours 30 minutes. How far does it go?
questions.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

hi.prompt: एक कार 60 किमी/घंटा की चाल से 2 घंटे 30 मिनट चलती है। वह कितनी दूरी तय करती है?

questions.prompt: ₹1200 is divided between two people in the ratio 3 : 5. What is the larger share?
questions.explanation: The parts total 3 + 5 = 8; the larger share is 5/8 × 1200 = ₹750.

hi.prompt: ₹1200 को दो व्यक्तियों में 3 : 5 के अनुपात में बाँटा जाता है। बड़ा हिस्सा कितना है?

questions.prompt: What is the simple interest on ₹5000 at 8% per year for 3 years?

hi.prompt: ₹5000 पर 8% वार्षिक दर से 3 वर्ष का साधारण ब्याज कितना होगा?

questions.prompt: A can finish a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together, how many days will they take?
questions.explanation: In one day they do 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 1/6 of the job, so together they take 6 days.

hi.prompt: A किसी काम को 10 दिन में और B उसे 15 दिन में पूरा कर सकता है। दोनों मिलकर कितने दिन में करेंगे?

questions.prompt: What comes next: 3, 9, 27, 81, …?
questions.explanation: Each term is 3 times the one before: 81 × 3 = 243.

hi.explanation: हर पद पिछले पद का 3 गुना है: 81 × 3 = 243।

questions.prompt: If CAT is written as DBU, how is DOG written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: C→D, A→B, T→U. So D→E, O→P, G→H gives EPH.

hi.prompt: यदि किसी कूट में CAT को DBU लिखा जाता है, तो उसी कूट में DOG को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
hi.explanation: हर अक्षर एक स्थान आगे जाता है: C→D, A→B, T→U। इसलिए D→E, O→P, G→H से EPH बनता है।

questions.prompt: Which number is the odd one out: 121, 144, 169, 180?
questions.explanation: 121 = 11², 144 = 12² and 169 = 13² are perfect squares; 180 is not.

questions.prompt: Meena walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is she from where she started?
questions.explanation: North 5 km, then east 3 km, then south 5 km brings her back level with the start, 3 km to the east.

hi.prompt: मीना 5 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलती है, फिर दाएँ मुड़कर 3 किमी चलती है, फिर दोबारा दाएँ मुड़कर 5 किमी चलती है। वह आरंभिक स्थान से कितनी दूर है?
hi.explanation: उत्तर 5 किमी, फिर पूर्व 3 किमी, फिर दक्षिण 5 किमी चलकर वह आरंभिक स्थान से ठीक 3 किमी पूर्व में पहुँचती है।

questions.prompt: Pointing to a boy, Asha says, "He is the son of my father's only son." How is the boy related to Asha?
questions.explanation: Asha is a woman, so her father's only son is her brother. The boy is her brother's son: her nephew.

hi.prompt: एक लड़के की ओर इशारा करते हुए आशा कहती है, "यह मेरे पिता के इकलौते बेटे का बेटा है।" लड़का आशा का क्या लगता है?
hi.explanation: आशा एक महिला है, इसलिए उसके पिता का इकलौता बेटा उसका भाई है। लड़का उसके भाई का बेटा यानी उसका भतीजा है।

sets.title: Class XII Mathematics: chapter-wise practice
sets.description: Original questions across the Class XII mathematics syllabus, from relations and functions to probability, in English and Hindi. Check your board's current syllabus for the exact chapter list.

questions.prompt: If f : R → R is given by f(x) = 3x + 2, what is f⁻¹(x)?
questions.explanation: Put y = 3x + 2, so x = (y − 2)/3. Hence f⁻¹(x) = (x − 2)/3.

hi.prompt: यदि f : R → R, f(x) = 3x + 2 द्वारा परिभाषित है, तो f⁻¹(x) क्या है?

questions.prompt: What is the principal value of sin⁻¹(−1/2)?
questions.explanation: The principal value of sin⁻¹ lies in [−π/2, π/2]. sin(−π/6) = −1/2, so the answer is −π/6.

hi.prompt: sin⁻¹(−1/2) का मुख्य मान क्या है?
hi.explanation: sin⁻¹ का मुख्य मान [−π/2, π/2] में होता है। sin(−π/6) = −1/2, इसलिए उत्तर −π/6 है।

questions.prompt: If A is a 2 × 3 matrix and B is a 3 × 4 matrix, what is the order of AB?
questions.explanation: AB is defined because A has 3 columns and B has 3 rows; AB has the rows of A and the columns of B: 2 × 4.

hi.prompt: यदि A एक 2 × 3 आव्यूह और B एक 3 × 4 आव्यूह है, तो AB की कोटि क्या है?
hi.explanation: A में 3 स्तंभ और B में 3 पंक्तियाँ हैं, इसलिए AB परिभाषित है; इसकी कोटि A की पंक्तियाँ × B के स्तंभ = 2 × 4 है।

questions.prompt: What is the value of the determinant |2 3; 1 4| (first row 2, 3; second row 1, 4)?

hi.prompt: सारणिक |2 3; 1 4| (पहली पंक्ति 2, 3; दूसरी पंक्ति 1, 4) का मान क्या है?

questions.prompt: A is a 3 × 3 matrix with |A| = 4. What is |2A|?
questions.explanation: For an n × n matrix, |kA| = kⁿ|A|. Here |2A| = 2³ × 4 = 32.

hi.prompt: A एक 3 × 3 आव्यूह है जिसके लिए |A| = 4 है। |2A| क्या है?
hi.explanation: n × n आव्यूह के लिए |kA| = kⁿ|A|। यहाँ |2A| = 2³ × 4 = 32।

questions.prompt: What is d/dx (sin x²)?
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, d/dx sin(u) = cos(u) · du/dx with u = x², so the derivative is 2x cos(x²).

hi.prompt: d/dx (sin x²) क्या है?
hi.explanation: शृंखला नियम से d/dx sin(u) = cos(u) · du/dx, जहाँ u = x²; अतः अवकलज 2x cos(x²) है।

questions.prompt: What is d/dx (e³ˣ)?
questions.explanation: d/dx e^(kx) = k e^(kx); with k = 3 the derivative is 3e³ˣ.

hi.prompt: d/dx (e³ˣ) क्या है?
hi.explanation: d/dx e^(kx) = k e^(kx); k = 3 रखने पर अवकलज 3e³ˣ है।

questions.prompt: At which point does f(x) = x³ − 3x have a local maximum?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 gives x = ±1. f″(x) = 6x is negative at x = −1, so f has a local maximum there (and a local minimum at x = 1).

hi.prompt: f(x) = x³ − 3x का स्थानीय उच्चिष्ठ किस बिंदु पर है?
hi.explanation: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 से x = ±1। f″(x) = 6x, x = −1 पर ऋणात्मक है, इसलिए वहाँ स्थानीय उच्चिष्ठ है (और x = 1 पर स्थानीय निम्निष्ठ)।
